overview.heading: Learning beyond the classroom.
overview.intro: Hustle Hive Alternative Provision offers small-group, hands-on learning in Darlington for young people in Years 6 to 11, commissioned by schools and local authorities.

why.heading: Why choose us?
paragraphs: Hustle Hive gives the young people you refer a calm, nurturing setting built around their individual needs. With up to six learners a day, staff know each young person well, and our approach supports academic progress and personal development together, with a focus on resilient mental health and transferable skills.

Learning is practical and tech-based, built around our Hustle 100 curriculum, so learners develop skills that matter beyond school. We agree targets with you at the start of a placement and report back on attendance, wellbeing and progress.
why.imageAlt: Students working on laptops beside a 3D printer at Hustle Hive

who.heading: Who do we work with?
who.intro: Hustle Hive may be right for young people in Years 6 to 11 who would benefit from a smaller, practical and highly structured learning environment as part of an agreed education plan.
points: Young people who are disengaging from mainstream learning, or whose attendance and participation are becoming a concern.
Learners who respond well to practical, project-based and vocationally relevant activities.
Young people who need to rebuild confidence, routine, motivation and positive relationships with adults.
Learners who may benefit from a smaller group and a calmer environment than a busy mainstream classroom.
Young people whose objectives include improving engagement, communication, independence, practical skills or readiness for reintegration or transition.
suitability: Suitability is considered individually. A referral isn't accepted just because a place is available: we need enough information about a learner's education, safeguarding, health, behaviour and support needs to be sure we can meet them safely and effectively.

Our small size means we can adapt day to day, but it doesn't mean we can meet every level of SEND, medical or behavioural need. Where specialist input is needed, we work with the commissioner and relevant professionals.
who.accessibility: Our Denmark Street premises is not currently wheelchair accessible. Accessibility, reasonable adjustments and any personal-care needs are considered carefully during referral.

offer.heading: Our Alternative Provision
paragraphs: Our alternative provision is designed to meet the needs of young people who may find conventional schooling challenging. We use a hands-on approach that brings together STEM, outdoor education and creative projects, from 3D printing and engineering to digital media.
Our dedicated educators work closely with students, making sure they get the individual attention they need to build confidence and skills, and prepare for future opportunities.
offer.imageAlt: A group of students hiking beside a lake with backpacks

approach.heading: Our approach & the Hustle 100
approach.intro: Regulate, relate, reason: how we support young people, what a day looks like, and the curriculum behind it.

resilience.heading: Supporting Mental Health & Resilience
resilience.intro: We understand that a young person's behaviour and engagement are often the visible signs of much deeper experiences of stress, disruption or trauma. So our sessions are built in a clear order.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Through movement, rhythm, routine and calm relationships.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Academic and practical learning, once a young person feels safe and settled.

resilience.frameworksIntro: Our approach is grounded in two complementary frameworks.

frameworks.name: The Power Threat Meaning Framework
frameworks.text: (Johnstone & Boyle, 2018) helps us move away from labelling young people by "what's wrong with them" and instead ask what has happened to them, so staff can respond with understanding rather than judgement.

frameworks.name: Dr Bruce Perry's Neurosequential Model of Therapeutics
frameworks.text: recognises that the brain develops and regulates in a specific sequence, from basic survival responses through to higher-level thinking and learning.

activities.heading: What our students do
activities.intro: We balance cutting-edge technology and entrepreneurship with ancient skills like bushcraft, mindfulness and wild wellness, using Darlington and the wider Tees Valley as our classroom. Every activity links to the Hustle 100.

items.title: 3D Print Challenge
items.text: Design a useful product in CAD, then prototype, test and improve it before printing the final version.

items.title: Product Design Challenge
items.text: Solve a real-world problem by researching, sketching, modelling and creating a prototype.

items.title: STEM Build Challenge
items.text: Teams take on a challenge like the strongest bridge, tallest tower or fastest vehicle.

items.title: Hustle Hive Market Day
items.text: Develop products, calculate costs, make stock and displays, then sell at a real mini market.

items.title: Dere Street Roman walk & Piercebridge Roman Fort
items.text: Linked to our Year 7 Roman Britain unit, with the group presenting a find or feature back at the fort.

items.title: Beach clean & coastal erosion survey
items.text: A litter audit and pick, leading to an upcycled beach-plastic mini-enterprise product.

items.title: Cleveland Mountain Rescue visit
items.text: A mini enterprise task: costing kit, designing a callout process and pitching improvements.

items.title: Roseberry Topping & Captain Cook's Monument
items.text: A hike in the Cleveland Hills.

day.intro: A calm, predictable structure, with a check-in at the start and a reflection at the end.
day.note: Mobile phones are handed in while on the premises, in line with current guidance.

timeline.title: Arrival & check-in
timeline.text: Settle in, attendance, wellbeing check and goals for the day.

timeline.title: Session 1
timeline.text: English and maths reinforced through practical projects, enterprise and wellbeing-focused learning, adapted to each learner's targets.

timeline.title: Session 2
timeline.text: STEM, design, digital making or enterprise.

timeline.text: Practical work, teamwork, problem solving and employability.

timeline.title: Reflection, review & departure

curriculum.heading: Our Unique Curriculum
paragraphs: We deliver a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum designed around each learner. Core academic development is combined with practical, real-world experiences that build confidence, resilience and essential life skills.

Learners keep developing literacy, numeracy, communication and problem-solving through meaningful projects, alongside enterprise, STEM, creative technologies, outdoor education, wellbeing and personal development.
curriculum.note: Through meaningful work experience and employer days, we can also help you better hit your Gatsby Benchmarks for hard-to-reach students.
curriculum.imageAlt: The Hustle 100 wheel showing its ten areas

hustle100.heading: The Hustle 100
paragraphs: Hustle 100 gives young people the chance to build real skills, confidence and life experience. Ten connected areas, each with ten challenges, help them grow, achieve and prepare for what's next. Learners don't need to complete all 100: each young person follows a flexible, personalised pathway that fits their needs, interests, placement objectives and length of placement.

Where appropriate, Hustle 100 activities can count towards recognised awards, unit accreditation and certificates of achievement, so even learners on shorter placements leave with tangible recognition.

ambition.heading: Our ambition for every learner
ambition.intro: For every learner to leave with greater confidence, new skills, positive experiences and a clearer sense of what they can achieve next. We track progress in six areas.

items.title: Engagement
items.text: More participation, willingness to try tasks, better learning stamina and fewer refusals or withdrawals.

items.title: Attendance
items.text: Better attendance at commissioned sessions, and improved routines around arrival, punctuality and readiness to learn.

items.title: Learning
items.text: Progress against agreed academic or practical targets, evidenced by completed work, observation and assessment.

items.title: Behaviour & regulation
items.text: A better ability to manage frustration, follow agreed expectations, repair relationships and use support strategies.

items.title: Confidence & communication
items.text: More willingness to ask for help, contribute, explain ideas, work with others and reflect on progress.

items.title: Transition readiness
items.text: Evidence the learner is better prepared for reintegration, a new placement, post-16 education, training or employment.

referrals.heading: Referral & placement
referrals.intro: We welcome conversations with schools, local-authority teams and other commissioners exploring whether Hustle Hive could be part of a young person's education package.
referrals.packText: Everything in one place: who we work with, our curriculum, a typical day, referral and placement planning, safeguarding, monitoring and reporting, SEND support, health and safety, our team and due diligence documents.

steps.title: Referral
steps.text: The commissioner shares education history, attendance, SEND, health, behaviour, safeguarding and risk information.

steps.title: Suitability discussion
steps.text: We review the information and talk with the commissioner about whether we can safely and appropriately meet the learner's needs.

steps.title: Meeting parents and carers
steps.text: A chance to build a positive, trusting relationship from the start, see the building and meet the staff.

steps.title: Placement agreement
steps.text: Together we agree days, hours, objectives, responsibilities, information-sharing, safeguarding escalation, attendance procedures, review dates and costs.

steps.title: Induction
steps.text: The learner is introduced to the environment, staff, routines, expectations, safety procedures and the purpose of the placement.

steps.title: Baseline and targets
steps.text: Strengths, needs and priorities are recorded and turned into a small number of measurable targets.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Progress, attendance, behaviour and suitability are reviewed at agreed intervals, with changes made when needed.

steps.title: Transition or exit
steps.text: The end of the placement is planned, with clear next steps and a summary of progress and recommendations.

agreed: Start date, expected duration and review dates

monitoring.heading: Safeguarding, monitoring & quality
attendance: Attendance is recorded for every session, and non-attendance is reported promptly to the commissioner.
Named contacts are agreed for Hustle Hive, parents and carers, and the commissioner.
Significant incidents are recorded and shared promptly. Urgent safeguarding, health or safety information is shared immediately.
Formal progress updates are provided at agreed review points.
quality: We record attendance, learning, Hustle 100 milestones, behaviour, wellbeing and placement outcomes, using a simple cycle of baseline, delivery, review and improvement.
If progress isn't on track, we'll raise it with you rather than let a placement continue without a clear purpose. External quality-assurance visits are welcomed.

pricing.heading: Exceptional value
pricing.text: Our £155 daily rate includes transport, snacks and refreshments, specialist facilities, learning resources and personalised support. With no hidden charges and everything included as standard, schools can be confident they are receiving a high-quality provision that offers excellent value for money.

items.q: What makes Hustle Hive different to other alternative provisions?
items.a: We balance cutting-edge technology and entrepreneurship with skills like bushcraft, mindfulness and wild wellness. Groups are small by design, learning is practical and purposeful, and everything is built around our Hustle 100 curriculum and a regulate, relate, reason approach.

items.q: Who is Hustle Hive suitable for?
items.a: Young people in Years 6 to 11 who would benefit from a smaller, practical and highly structured learning environment as part of an agreed education plan. Key Stages are taught separately.

items.q: How many students attend each day?
items.a: Up to 6 learners per day, so staff can know each young person well and respond quickly when needs change.
Yes. Transport is included in our £155 daily rate, along with snacks and refreshments. Lunch can be provided by agreement.

items.q: How do schools make a referral?
items.a: Contact Gavin or Kieron to discuss a placement. We'll ask for the learner's education, attendance, SEND, health, behaviour, safeguarding and risk information, then talk through suitability. See "Referral & placement" above for the full process.
